teaser: First the database went, now the back end: the SGit Newsroom runs all its logic in the browser, on commodity servers that cannot read your data.
core_idea: After replacing the database with the file system (LETS), the next step is removing the back end: encrypted vaults make the server blind, so the application moves to the browser, leaving only commodity products on the server side; the security gaps this leaves are written down and accepted because they do not match the threat, and the result scales without its complexity scaling and ships as files.

nodes.label: The file system is the database
nodes.summary: LETS: load, extract, transform, save; every state a file you can version and read.

nodes.label: No back end
nodes.summary: All application logic runs in the reader's browser.

nodes.label: A blind server
nodes.summary: Vaults are encrypted in the client, so anything that reads data must run where the key is.

nodes.label: Commodity servers, not no servers
nodes.summary: Static hosting, a ciphertext store, a payment link, DNS and CI, with a sign-in provider next, all products.

nodes.label: The SGit Newsroom
nodes.summary: Personas, a reading meter, a payment on-ramp, a newsroom of your own, encrypted sharing, in-browser databases.

nodes.label: Gaps written down and accepted
nodes.summary: SG Meter's security model: every cheat changes a number only the cheater sees.

nodes.label: Scales without complexity scaling
nodes.summary: More readers add bandwidth against cached files, not moving parts.

nodes.label: A release is a set of files
nodes.summary: 114 releases in eleven days; the meter in seven releases in an afternoon.

nodes.label: Sovereignty, privacy, explainability, determinism
nodes.summary: The pattern's properties, not its policies.

nodes.label: How far can it be pushed?
nodes.summary: Secrets the reader must not hold are the honest boundary.

quotes.text: Encryption came first, and the client-side architecture followed, because there was nowhere else for the logic to go.
First the database went, and the work got simpler. Now the back end is going, and the work is getting faster.
